summary: Vasily Vasilyev was a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Kazan Federal University (~1834–1837) and held a post at the Russian Ecclesiastical Mission in Beijing (~1840–1850).

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Principal and Professor of Sanskrit at Morris College (~1942–1947) and Government Vidarbha Institute (~1947–1952), later becoming Hony. Professor at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (~1957–1966).

Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale studied at the University of Bonn (PhD ~1928–1930), working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and sinology. He held posts at Fergusson College (~1932–1957), Visva-Bharati University (~1937–1939), and the University of Delhi (~1964–1966).

Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at the University of Madras, the University of Mumbai, and Harvard University (~1974–1978), and became Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida (~1982).
Velcheru Narayana Rao is an Indology scholar who served as Associate Professor of South Asian Studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1971–2008) and held a post at the University of Chicago.
Verity Harte is a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1986–1994). She held posts at King's College London (~1996–2005) and Yale University (~2005).

Vesna A. Wallace specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies, completing her doctorate at UC Berkeley (~1990–1995). She held posts at UC Berkeley (~1995–1999), Oxford (~2008–2010), and UC Santa Barbara (~2008).

Victor B. Lieberman is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Yale University (~1963–1967) and SOAS University of London (~1971–1976). He served as a professor at the University of Michigan (~1984–2022).

Victor Chan is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the University of Chicago. Around 2005, he became Executive Director of the Contemporary Tibetan Studies Program at the University of British Columbia.

Victor Forte is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Japanology who completed his Ph.D. at Temple University in 2004. Around 2004, he became Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Albright College.

Victor H. Mair worked in sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, studying at Dartmouth, SOAS, and Harvard. He held posts at Harvard University (~1976–1979) and the University of Pennsylvania (1980).
Victor Henry was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at École Centrale de Lille and the University of Paris (1888).

Victor Turner was a scholar in religious studies and other fields. He studied at University College London (~1946–1949) and the University of Manchester (~1949–1955), later chairing the Committee on Social Thought at the University of Chicago (~1968–1977).

Victoria Sujata is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Harvard University (~2000). She studied under Michael Aris and a committee including Leonard van der Kuijp, Robert M. Gimello, Dan Martin, and E. Gene Smith.

Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He served at Visva-Bharati University (~1907–1934) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1934–1942).
Vidya Dehejia is a scholar of history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Cambridge (~1961–1968) and held a post at Columbia University (~1982).

Vidya Niwas Mishra was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad and Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University (~1957–1960), later serving as Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1986).

Vilhelm Thomsen was a linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Randers State School and the University of Copenhagen (~1859–1869). He later served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen (~1887–1913).
Vincent Arthur Smith was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1900) and held a post at the University of Oxford (~1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University, Taisho University, Kyoto University, and Hanazono University under Lucia Dolce, and served as a research fellow at Leiden University in 2012.
